decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core airfield control business, it likely meets or stays near aspiration and its system and service complementarities justify keeping it.

The training program fits the firm's service model and installed-base support, so organisational slack supports retention, although weaker-than-expected uptake could lead to absorption into broader services.

This narrower training course is more exposed to demand shortfalls and easier to redeploy than hardware or software products, but it still complements the core lighting business enough to keep for now.

Airport collaboration software matches the firm's stated move toward integrated, real-time and collaborative airport operations, so management would continue backing it unless results clearly fall below aspiration.

As a flagship surveillance product aligned with the firm's future direction, it would receive continued managerial attention and resources, making withdrawal unlikely without a clear performance failure.
